statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - New Zealand Companies Register (www.companies.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English characters; te reo Maori names are permissible subject to cultural sensitivity review by the Registrar; every New Zealand company must include 'Limited' or 'Ltd' as the last word of its name; names must not be identical or almost identical to any existing registered or reserved company name under Section 22 of the Companies Act 1993.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name by the Registrar under Section 22 of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant may: (1) resubmit a revised application incorporating written consent from the relevant Minister or regulatory authority for restricted words; (2) file a formal request for administrative review by the Registrar of Companies within 20 working days of the rejection notice; (3) file fresh incorporation papers with a new distinctive element; and (4) apply to the High Court of New Zealand for judicial review of the Registrar's decision in accordance with the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted solely as a correspondence and administrative service address; however, a physical New Zealand street address must be designated as the registered office under Section 214 of the Companies Act 1993 for service of process, and each director must maintain a physical service address under Section 201 of the Companies Act 1993. A virtual office address cannot satisfy the physical registered office requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - approximately 3-5% annual probability for a low-risk, license-exempt digital webtoon publisher with no cash-intensive business operations; AML/CFT compliance records and customer due diligence files must nonetheless be retained for at least 7 years and be available for unannounced FMA or Companies Office inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), as amended; particularly ss 10 (constitution), 12-16 (application and registration), 17-21 (effect of registration), 38 (no par value), 122 (board resolutions), 128 (signing of documents), 161 (consent to act as director), and 332-348 (overseas/companies not registered domestically, as applicable); Companies (Fees) Regulations 2014.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (NZ Companies Register online form, commonly referred to as Form 1).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: New Zealand has no minimum paid-up or issued capital requirement under the Companies Act 1993. Shares are issued without par value, and the consideration for shares may be deferred, partly paid, or fully paid as determined by the directors. No escrow account rule, capital verification, or share premium escrow is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, by unanimous written resolution of the first board of directors of the company, in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 and the company's constitution, as follows:
1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The board hereby approves the allotment and issue of 100 fully paid ordinary shares to [Founding Shareholder Name], in consideration of a capital contribution of USD 100.00 (or such amount as the directors determine), such shares having no par value under New Zealand law. The share register shall be updated accordingly.
2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The registered office of the company shall be [Registered Office Address, City, New Zealand], and the address for service shall be [Service Address, City, New Zealand]. The directors are authorised to take all actions necessary to notify the Registrar of Companies and to maintain such addresses in the Companies Register.
3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: [Director A Name] is appointed as Director and Chairperson; [Director B Name], if any, is appointed as Director; [Company Secretary Name], if any, is appointed as Company Secretary; and [Authorised Signatory Name] is appointed as authorised signatory for banking, commercial contracts, payment processor agreements, and statutory filings.
4. ADMINISTRATIVE AUTHORITY: Each director and officer is authorised, jointly or singly, to execute any agreements, consents, and filings necessary to give full effect to these resolutions.
This resolution is effective immediately and is recorded in the company's minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register (https://register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a company name availability search on the Companies Register. Reserve the proposed company name online using the RealMe authenticated portal. Ensure the name does not contravene the Companies Act 1993, is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing name, and does not imply Crown affiliation, criminal activity, or any prohibited purpose. If a restricted word is used, obtain prior written consent from the relevant regulatory authority.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and one alternate name
Name availability search record
Written consent for any restricted word or designation (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused because the name is unavailable or misleading, select an alternative name and file a new reservation. If the refusal is based on a restricted word, obtain the requisite consent or revise the name. A rejected reservation may be re-submitted without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Incorporation Application and Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office; directors, shareholders, and any registered office nominee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the incorporation application, adopt or confirm the company constitution (standard or custom), and prepare the directors' consent to act and shareholder subscription letter. Verify director eligibility: every director must be a natural person aged 18 or older and must not be disqualified under Companies Act 1993, ss 151-152. Sign the application and consents; have the registered office provider sign consent to use the registered office address. If documents are executed overseas, arrange notarisation or apostille if requested by the Companies Office.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Registration of a Company (Form 1)
Constitution of the company, if custom constitution is adopted
Consent to act as director, signed by each proposed director
Shareholder subscription letter and consent to issue shares
Consent from registered office provider or landlord
Certified identification documents of directors/shareholders (if required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a query or requisition, provide the requested clarification or corrected document within 15 working days. Missing signatures or incomplete consents are cured by re-submitting the relevant signed page through the Companies Register. No additional registration fee is payable if the original application fee remains valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission, Payment, and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed application online via the Companies Register using a RealMe login. Pay the prescribed filing fee of NZD 65.00 electronically. Upon successful review, the Registrar registers the company, issues the electronic Certificate of Incorporation, allocates the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), and publishes the company details on the public register. Verify the registration date, entity number, and registered office details.
required_dossiers: Signed incorporation application as submitted online
Electronic payment confirmation of NZD 65.00 filing fee
Company constitution and signed consents, if not incorporated by reference
Valid RealMe authentication evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, the Registrar will provide written reasons. Correct the specified deficiencies and re-submit the application within any stated deadline. The refund or transfer of the filing fee is at the Registrar's discretion where no service has been performed, but in the ordinary course the corrected application proceeds without an extra fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convening of First Board Meeting and Establishment of Statutory Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company directors and shareholders; New Zealand Companies Office for mandatory filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a first board meeting or pass a written resolution in accordance with the constitution and Companies Act 1993. Adopt the First Board Resolution covering share allotment, registered office adoption, and officer appointments. Open and maintain the statutory registers: shareholders register, directors register, interests register, and minute book. If a director or officer changes within the first days, file the relevant notice with the Companies Office.
required_dossiers: Notice of first meeting or written resolution circulation record
First Board Resolution duly signed
Consent to act as each officer
Statutory registers (shareholder, director, interest, minutes)
Notice of appointment of directors, if required by the Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director's consent is invalid or an officer is incorrectly identified, pass a corrective board resolution and re-file the appointment notice with the Companies Office. Any late filing penalty can be avoided by filing promptly upon discovery; non-compliance is remedied by voluntary disclosure and correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax Registration and Ancillary Operational Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD); Fire and Emergency New Zealand; local territorial authority; WorkSafe New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with the Inland Revenue Department to obtain an IRD number and confirm tax residency status. Register for GST if the company's taxable supplies exceed the NZD 60,000 threshold or in minor cases where voluntary registration is chosen. If physical premises are occupied, ensure compliance with the Building Act 2004, the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, and any applicable local zoning consent. Submit applications for any required building warrant of fitness or fire evacuation scheme, and maintain worker engagement records.
required_dossiers: IRD company registration form or online registration through myIR
GST registration application (IR596 or online)
Lease agreement or title evidence for the registered office
Building compliance schedule and warrant of fitness application (if physical premises have specified systems)
Fire evacuation scheme application (if triggered by use or occupancy)
Health and safety due diligence and worker engagement records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD registration is delayed, use the public NZBN data through the Inland Revenue pre-fill service. If a building consent or fire safety certificate is refused by the local authority, request a reconsideration, amend the premises, or obtain alternative compliance documentation from a building inspector or engineered assessment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no statutory industrial licensing board regulates ISIC 9000 digital webtoon publishing in New Zealand. General workplace health and safety is administered by WorkSafe New Zealand and MBIE.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no operating licence or manufacturing permit is required for digital webtoon publishing, multilingual chapter unlocking, or digital content syndication. Payment processor merchant registration, Apple IAP, and Google Play Billing agreements are commercial contracts rather than state-issued licences.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not triggered — local territorial authority under the Resource Management Act 1991; central Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) applies only to hazardous substances or nationally significant proposals.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / No mandatory EIA — pure digital publishing has no listed activity under applicable RMA schedule categories and involves no physical production facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, particulate, or hazardous waste discharge arises from webtoon syndication. If a physical office or server suite is occupied, comply with local council stormwater and waste-minimisation bylaws under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008; electronic waste must be disposed of through an authorised e-waste recycler.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No industrial civil-defence licence is required for a digital-content company. For any physical office, maintain a building warrant of fitness for specified systems (fire alarms, emergency lighting, sprinklers) under the Building Act 2004; comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 by establishing a safe work environment, hazard register, and worker engagement process. Fire and Emergency New Zealand evacuation scheme registration is required only if the premises falls within the prescribed occupancy and use classes.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake), New Zealand's national tax authority; official website: https://www.ird.govt.nz; secure taxpayer portal: myIR Secure Online Services (https://myir.ird.govt.nz).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1 - APPOINTMENT AND DOCUMENTATION: The non-resident International Company (CK_IC) must appoint a New Zealand tax agent or authorised New Zealand representative for service of notices and assemble: Certificate of Incorporation; Memorandum and Articles of Association (or equivalent constitutional instruments); certificate of good standing or extract from the foreign company register; register extract identifying directors and ultimate beneficial owners; AML/CFT identification documents; and a board resolution authorising the NZ tax registration. STEP 2 - IRD NUMBER APPLICATION: Submit form IR742 'Non-Resident Company IRD Number Application' to Inland Revenue, declaring the entity's legal name, country of incorporation, registered address, NZ agent contact, details of all directors and beneficial owners, and the intended scope of NZ activities (for this IC: digital webtoon syndication, no NZ physical establishment). STEP 3 - ISSUANCE: Inland Revenue issues a unique 8-9 digit IRD number (the statutory tax file number) within approximately 5-15 business days. STEP 4 - GST REGISTRATION ANALYSIS: Apply for GST registration via myIR or form GST1 if (a) the IC supplies remote services to New Zealand resident consumers in excess of NZD 60,000 in any rolling 12-month period and those supplies are not collected by a marketplace operator, or (b) the IC voluntarily registers (section 54B, GST Act 1985) to recover input tax. Where all NZ consumer sales flow through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, the marketplace operators are the deemed GST suppliers for NZ consumer sales; the IC's supply to Apple/Google is a zero-rated B2B export and the IC is not required to register for NZ GST. STEP 5 - ONGOING MAINTENANCE: Update the IRD record within 30 days of any change in directors, NZ agent, registered address, or beneficial ownership; retain the IRD number confirmation, GST registration certificate (if any), and all supporting registration evidence in the corporate statutory records for 7 years.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (per the ELF_CUSTOM_CK_IC classification model). In New Zealand statutory terms, CK_IC is a non-resident foreign company taxed only on New Zealand-sourced income (source-based taxation under the Income Tax Act 2007, source rules in sections YD 4 and YD 5). Digital webtoon publishing and multilingual chapter-unlocking income derived from offshore consumers, Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, and non-resident syndication licensees constitutes foreign-sourced income and is excluded from the NZ income tax base absent a New Zealand permanent establishment, a NZ-resident agent concluding contracts on the IC's behalf, or income attributable to NZ activities. The IC is therefore not subject to the 28% NZ corporate income tax rate on its offshore business profits. Any NZ-source income (e.g., direct B2C digital sales to NZ consumers not intermediated by a marketplace operator, or NZ-sourced royalties from a NZ licensee) would be subject to NZ non-resident withholding tax, generally at the 15% treaty/NRWT rate, and any such direct consumer supplies would trigger NZ GST registration at the NZD 60,000 threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box entity classification regime; classification follows statute. Available elections for CK_IC include: (1) GST registration and filing period elections under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985: monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly return periods (section 16); payments-basis vs invoice-basis accounting (section 19); voluntary GST registration (section 51); and GST grouping with a NZ-resident group company (joint election under section 55). (2) Hybrid and branch mismatch elections under Part GC of the Income Tax Act 2007 (inserted by the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018): where a payment or entity is treated differently in New Zealand and the counterparty jurisdiction, the IC may elect the OECD-conform compensatory adjustment to neutralise a double non-taxation outcome and must maintain contemporaneous hybrid mismatch documentation and lodge any required IRD disclosure schedules. (3) Balance date election: the IC may elect a non-standard accounting balance date, with Commissioner's approval, to align its NZ reporting with the offshore shareholder's balance date (Income Tax Act 2007, sections 38-39). (4) For GST, the IC may adopt the 'deemed zero-rated export' administrative treatment for remote services supplied to non-resident recipients, recording the recipient's non-resident status contemporaneously. (5) If the IC subsequently acquires a NZ GST-registered subsidiary or branch, it may elect GST cross-border and group elections to neutralise inter-company GST. No check-the-box election is available to treat the IC as a disregarded or transparent entity for NZ purposes; the IC is a taxable person in its own right for GST and a non-resident company for income tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) - a value-added tax administered under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (New Zealand GST; functionally equivalent to a VAT).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000. Threshold rules: (i) Domestic nexus: any person carrying on a taxable activity must register for GST when the total value of taxable supplies in any 12-month period exceeds NZD 60,000, or has a reasonable expectation of doing so. (ii) Offshore remote-services nexus: from 1 October 2016, a non-resident supplier of 'remote services' (which includes digital webtoon content, chapter unlocks, and digital subscriptions) to New Zealand resident consumers must register when the aggregate value of those supplies to NZ consumers exceeds NZD 60,000 in any rolling 12-month period. (iii) Marketplace exception: where CK_IC's remote services are supplied to NZ consumers through an electronic marketplace (Apple App Store via Apple IAP and Google Play via Google Play Billing), the marketplace operator is the deemed supplier and is liable for NZ GST on those NZ consumer sales (marketplace operator rules, sections 8C, 8D, and 60C of the GST Act 1985), subject to the same NZD 60,000 threshold applied to the operator's NZ supplies. (iv) The NZD 60,000 threshold is measured on a GST-exclusive consideration basis; registration is compulsory from the day after the threshold is crossed and an application must be filed within 21 days (administrative practice for non-residents). (v) Voluntary registration is available to non-residents even below the threshold to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, digital stamping, or pre-clearance API mandate for e-invoices. GST returns (form GST101) are filed electronically through the myIR portal, and GST liabilities are paid electronically by direct debit or bank transfer. Electronic invoicing through the PEPPOL network is voluntary in NZ (adopted 2022 for B2G interoperability) and is not a statutory precondition for input tax deduction; a valid tax invoice under the GST Act 1985 may be issued in paper or electronic form. There is no requirement for third-party fiscal certification of cash registers or invoicing software. CK_IC should nevertheless implement a compliant electronic invoicing workflow (issuing tax invoices or documentation for zero-rated exports, retaining marketplace settlement reports, and preserving 7 years of records) and, if voluntarily registered, should use the myIR portal's GST101 e-filing and integrate its accounting records with digital platform data for audit readiness.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: CK_IC's digital webtoon publishing and multilingual chapter unlocking is a supply of 'remote services' (Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, section 8(4B)) and is zero-rated as an export under section 11(1)(m) where: (1) the recipient is non-resident and is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed (for digital content, deemed performed where the recipient is located, so an end-consumer outside NZ satisfies this test); (2) if the recipient is a NZ GST-registered person, the supply must not be made in connection with that recipient's NZ taxable activity, or the recipient has supplied its NZ GST number and declared that the services are wholly for its NZ taxable activity, in which case the supply is zero-rated under the B2B cross-border services rule. Specific application: (a) Sales through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing to offshore end-consumers: zero-rated; the platform operator is a non-resident recipient and the underlying supply to the operator is zero-rated; (b) Sales through Apple/Google to NZ end-consumers: not CK_IC's supply for GST purposes - the marketplace operator accounts for 15% GST on the NZ consumer sale, while CK_IC's platform settlement remains zero-rated; (c) Direct B2B licensing of the webtoon catalogue to non-resident syndication platforms, publishers, or aggregators: zero-rated under section 11(1)(m) upon receipt of the licensee's written non-resident declaration (name, address, foreign VAT/GST registration number where applicable, and confirmation that the services are not for a NZ taxable activity); (d) Direct B2C subscriptions to overseas readers via CK_IC's own website: zero-rated where geolocation, billing address, and payment method evidence conclusively places the consumer outside NZ. No GST refund arises on a zero-rated export because output tax is charged at 0%; input tax credits (e.g., on production software procured in NZ) are claimable only by a GST-registered person, so a non-registered IC would not file refund claims. If CK_IC voluntarily registers for GST, it may file monthly or six-monthly refund claims for NZ input tax attributable to export production inputs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CUSDEC) - formally not applicable to intangible digital remote services; New Zealand Customs does not process digital cross-border supplies, and zero-rating is evidenced by the GST exporter's records rather than a customs entry.

Bill of Lading / Air Waybill - not applicable to digital webtoon syndication; for any physical promotional goods (e.g., graphic albums or merchandise) shipped out of NZ, retain the shipping document to substantiate the goods-export zero-rating.

Digital platform settlement reports from Apple App Store Connect and Google Play Console evidencing gross revenues, platform commissions, app and territory breakdowns, and the non-NZ status of transacting consumers.
Geolocation, IP-address logs, device country codes, and billing-address records from the chapter-unlocking server demonstrating that each end-consumer transaction is consummated outside New Zealand.

Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or SWIFT/PSP settlement records from Apple, Google, and banking institutions evidencing actual receipt of offshore export proceeds within the 180-day repatriation window.

Executed B2B non-resident declaration forms from each non-resident licensee or platform operator, including the recipient's foreign VAT/GST registration certificate where available, confirming offshore consumption and non-resident status.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue audits export zero-rating by focusing on the 'remote services' rules, marketplace operator attribution, and transfer pricing. If CK_IC or its marketplace operator misapplies zero-rating (e.g., the IC cannot substantiate that a consumer was outside NZ, or supplies to NZ consumers were incorrectly zero-rated on the IC's direct sales), Inland Revenue will: (1) reassess output GST at 15% on the full taxable value of the wrongly zero-rated supplies; (2) impose use-of-money interest (UOMI) on the resulting GST shortfall at the prescribed quarterly rate (historically between 8% and 10.5% for underpayment); and (3) assess shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for lack of reasonable care; 20% for an unacceptable tax position; 20% for a tax avoidance arrangement; 100% for an abusive tax position; and 150% for evasion or an equivalent offence. In cases involving false documentation (e.g., fabricated non-resident declarations or forged IRCs), criminal prosecution is available with fines of up to NZD 50,000 per offence and imprisonment of up to 5 years (Tax Administration Act 1994, sections 143A, 143B, and 144). Retrospective assessments may be raised within the 4-year amendment period under section 108 of the Tax Administration Act 1994; there is no time limit where the defect arises from fraud or evasion. Any clawback of zero-rated export treatment would reduce input tax credits proportionately and could trigger consequential adjustments to marketplace operator attribution. CK_IC must therefore retain all platform, geolocation, and remittance evidence for at least 7 years and implement a documented zero-rating substantiation matrix for immediate production in audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), acting as the apex monetary authority for NZD clearing and settlement, with supervisory coordination from the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) in respect of the Cook Islands International Company registration and any regulated financial activity in Rarotonga.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a free-floating exchange rate regime with full current-account and capital-account convertibility under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 and the Currency and Bank Notes Act. There are no statutory exchange control approvals for the conversion of NZD, no profit-remittance gatekeeping by the RBNZ, and no restrictions on the disposal of dividends, royalties, or loan repayments by non-resident entities. The Cook Islands IC, being a tax-exempt non-resident, can freely repatriate platform settlement proceeds; however, all remittances are screened under the AML/CFT Act 2009, the AML/CFT Regulations 2011 (which impose originator and beneficiary information obligations for wire transfers at or above NZD 1,000), and FATCA/CRS self-certification protocols. The only practical hurdle is documentary: the paying bank must obtain the entity's non-resident status, beneficial ownership declaration, and evidence that no New Zealand permanent establishment is created under the domestic PE test, as there is no comprehensive double taxation agreement between New Zealand and the Cook Islands.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export or digital-service receipts in New Zealand; exporters may hold foreign currency indefinitely in any deliverable currency. For the webtoon syndication scope, proceeds remitted from Apple IAP and Google Play arrive as USD gross-settlement after store commissions, and the receiving NZ bank will automate the FX conversion to NZD only upon the company's explicit instruction, at the then-prevailing interbank mid-rate plus an agreed spread. All receipts above NZD 10,000 trigger enhanced monitoring under the AMLCFT obliged-entity obligations, which requires an audit trail linking the platform payout statement to the inbound credit.

Operational Account dedicated to Apple/Google settlement sweeps; separate digital-exporter acceleration desk

Operational Account (limited offshore IC appetite; retail-centric)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for daily low-value USD/NZD sweeps from Apple IAP and Google Play via regulated New Zealand-registered e-money and payment institutions, provided the EMI is registered on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) and maintains an AML/CFT compliance programme approved by the Department of Internal Affairs. Leading entities such as Wise and Airwallex (NZ branch) can accept a Cook Islands International Company after a four-to-eight-week onboarding cycle, subject to the same beneficial-ownership disclosure as Tier-1 banks. Critical legal constraint: an unlicensed offshore EMI, for example a UK or Lithuania e-money institution without NZ FSPR registration, cannot lawfully provide payment services in New Zealand without either registration or a recognised exemption under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Disputes Resolution) Act 2008; engaging a foreign EMI without NZ passporting creates licensing and sanctions risk for the treasury mandate.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permissible under the AML/CFT Act 2009 using an electronic identity verification (eIV) provider when the customer risk rating is low; however, the Cook Islands IC legal form is routinely treated as higher-risk, which induces most Tier-1 banks and EMIs to require a live video-conference KYC interview with at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner, and BNZ or ANZ may condition final onboarding on a physical countersignature in Auckland by the signatory who holds New Zealand proof-of-identity. A physical in-person interview is not a statutory mandate, but it is a practical bank policy for offshore-flagged ICs; the treasury should prepare a certified board resolution, two independent directors' passports, and a notarised trust deed in advance to shorten the biometric verification window.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: Cook Islands International Companies are non-transparent in public registries, which raises the shadow of hidden control under NZ AML/CFT Section 33 customer due diligence expectations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation under the International Companies Act; notarised register of directors and members; full trust deed and trustee consent if the IC is held under a trust; beneficial-ownership template certified by the Cook Islands FSC; legal opinion of an NZ-licensed counsel confirming tax-exempt-zone status; three-month bank reference from an existing professional counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction association: Cook Islands appears on FATF monitoring lists and EU non-cooperative tax-haven annexes, triggering automatic enhanced due diligence and counterparty de-risking by NZ banks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Economic-substance file: registered-office agreement in Cook Islands or NZ trust-company address; utility or office lease evidence; board minutes of operational decisions in Rarotonga; detailed digital-publishing business plan; signed Apple Developer Program agreement and Google Play Console payout terms; enhanced due diligence questionnaire responses listing counterparties and projected monthly settlement volume.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Settlement-rails mismatch: declared ISIC 9000 digital publishing revenue routed through Apple IAP and Google Play appears as third-party platform settlement rather than classic trade invoices, creating unusual transaction patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly App Store Connect payout statements in USD; Google Play financial reconciliation reports; subcontractor contracts for multilingual chapter localisation; end-user licence agreements; artist royalty ledger; app-store analytics exports to reconcile revenue wave with treasury inflows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency mismatch: the IC claims tax-exempt status but banks suspect the New Zealand permanent establishment threshold is breached due to platform management in Auckland.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: NZ IRD non-resident company filing declaration or exemption certificate; board-meeting locus demonstrated by minutes held in Cook Islands; physical-absence policy describing no NZ employment functions; economic-substance declaration to the Cook Islands FSC; conclusion-of-fact memo applying New Zealand domestic permanent-establishment tests and confirming the absence of a fixed place of business.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfer from the settlor or parent with the purpose narrative 'Equity injection by share subscription under the International Companies Act'; the receiving NZ bank requires a pre-approved capital file containing the IC share issuance resolution, a subscription ledger, source-of-wealth statements, and confirmation of the registered office. Alternative routing through the Cook Islands trustee's segregated account at ANZ Rarotonga or BNZ Auckland office must reference the trust name and be accompanied by the trust deed; funds then flow via MT202 for interbank settlement into the IC operational account. Verification steps: sanctions and PEP screening on the remitter, confirmation code via SWIFT-GPI tracker, and posting of the CRS/FATCA self-certification form for the IC as a passive non-financial entity with controlling person disclosure.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Daily white-labelled royalty payouts to freelance artists use preferred rails of batch MT103 files through the host bank's API or the SWIFT Global Payment Innovation (GPI) service; for physical print merchandise procurement from Asian printers, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (MT700) is the standard clearing rail, with documents negotiated through a confirming bank in Shanghai or Singapore; intercompany treasury prompts to the parent trust use MT202 or MT202COV cover payments to avoid double-charging. All NZD disbursements clear in real time on the RBNZ Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) with a T+0 finality window, while USD legs settle on the CHIPS or CLS New York window with next-day availability; any counterparty in sanctioned territories is screened out via SWIFT sanctions-list filtering prior to instruction release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Outright Forwards (NZD/USD) with tenors up to 12 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with the Tier-1 banker
FX Swaps (NZD/USD same-day and tomorrow-next rollovers) for management of settlement window mismatches
European-style Vanilla FX Options (NZD/USD engaged puts and call spreads) permitting upside participation on webtoon season launch peaks
Cross-Currency Basis Swaps (NZD/USD CCIRS) for converting long-term USD platform receivables into NZD funding certainty

Offshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (USD/CNH and USD/CNY NDFs) authorised solely for hedging Chinese-language licensing counterparty settlement risk where onshore CNY deliverability is restricted; NZD NDFs are not required because NZD is fully deliverable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form 8) - company and shareholder confirmation under the Companies Act 1993, s 224
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the company's Annual Return Date (ARF). If a balance date has been notified to the Registrar, the ARF is the last day of the balance period (commonly 31 March); otherwise the ARF is the incorporation anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence: company and every director liable to a daily fine not exceeding NZD 10 (approx. USD 6) per day of continuing default. After 12 months of non-filing, the Registrar may issue a strike-off notice under s 318 of the Companies Act 1993, leading to administrative removal from the New Zealand register unless a valid objection is lodged.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial statements and auditor's report (if audited) under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, ss 20-25
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and shareholders (preparation); New Zealand Companies Office (filing for large companies and FMC reporting entities through the annual-return digital portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Preparation must be completed within 5 months after balance date; entities required to file deliver the statements to the Companies Office by the annual-return filing deadline. A compulsory audit, where triggered, must be completed before filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company and every director in default are liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding NZD 50,000 (approx. USD 31,000) under the Financial Reporting Act 2013. Repeated non-compliance also constitutes grounds for strike-off under s 318 of the Companies Act 1993.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Significant Individual Register (UBO) annual confirmation - Companies Amendment Act 2021, Part 8A
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (completeness declaration embedded in the annual return; no separate filing form)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration submitted with the annual return within 20 working days after the Annual Return Date. Internal register amendments must be entered within 10 working days of any share transfer or change in significant control.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or update the register, or knowingly making a false entry, is an offence carrying a fine up to NZD 50,000 (approx. USD 31,000). The Registrar may also issue a compliance notice and, for continued breach, commence strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is triggered if (1) the entity qualifies as 'large': total assets exceed NZD 60M (approx. USD 37M), total revenue exceeds NZD 30M (approx. USD 19M), or the entity has 50+ full-time equivalent employees; (2) the entity is an FMC reporting entity (issuer of publicly offered financial products); or (3) shareholders holding 5% or more of voting rights request an audit within 60 days after balance date. Small and medium companies not meeting these conditions are exempt from compulsory audit under s 36 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Tier 1: NZ IFRS (IFRS as adopted by New Zealand); Tier 2: NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime; Tier 3: Simpler NZ GAAP; Tier 4: Special-purpose framework for small owner-managed entities. All companies must prepare financial statements in accordance with the Financial Reporting Act 2013.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: As at the Annual Return Date, the board must review the internal Significant Individual Register (SIR) and declare its accuracy within the annual return. A significant individual is any person owning more than 25% of shares or voting control, or exercising significant influence over the company. Each share transfer resulting in a new reportable beneficial owner must be entered in the SIR within 10 working days; the annual-return declaration attests to the register's currency.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Share Register) - Companies Act 1993, s 89
Register of Directors - Companies Act 1993, s 89
Register of Charges - Companies Act 1993, s 102
Significant Individual Register (UBO Register) - Companies Amendment Act 2021, Part 8A
Minute Book (directors' and shareholders' resolutions) - Companies Act 1993, ss 172 and 192

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - 2,400 per annum (NZD 1,200 - 3,800) covering registered office services, statutory agent correspondence, annual-return preparation, and register maintenance via a licensed New Zealand corporate-services provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 18,000 per annum (NZD 8,000 - 28,000) for a small-to-medium cross-border digital content licensing entity; zero if the small-company audit exemption under s 36 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013 is validly elected
